title: As anyone made any money from claude
author: needalltheprayers
selftext: Has anyone made money using claude? Have you made a trading bot or an app? If so, how was your experience? What would you advice on others who may want to do the same?

comments.author: Ok-Draft2744
comments.body:
I am yet to find a receipt that involes AI and works well. Not all lose money, and you can tailor its rules so it exits quickly if the market starts turning against you. All with the prompt. 

I find that standard bots that fully rely on Claude do not work. See traderank.ai as an example, most models lose money reliably. 

I think some sort of a combination of a strategy/algo + llm, might work. You will need extensive exploration and testing to verify that. 

The biggest win is probably learning a lot about llms if you decide to research it. 

Others might have different experiences, potentially more successful

replies.author: ilikerolls
replies.body:
I agree with this guy mostly. I wouldn’t rely on AI atm at least to write your strategy. Keep your strategy simple with an Entry Signal & a confirmation. You’d be surprised at how often an old easy strategy works with the right exit rules. Those ICT guys blow my mind with the complexity & trying to explain every reason why someone’s trade didn’t work.

You can ask Claude if u like as a starting point what strategies work on a certain symbol. If you’re new to Algo trading. The stuff that AI comes in handy for me is creating my actual “Trading System”. For instance I had Claude create a feature for my code that would detect Live “Strategy Decay”(when the Entry pattern I’m looking for is no longer valid before breaking my bank 😂).

My background is more in programming, systems engineering, Algorithms, & ML. Not so much in AI chat, but here’s what’s worked for me anyways. Create a Project with your basic 2 Entry confirmation strategy code. Prompt AI chat in a detailed outline of what you want it to do. I’m sure someone more familiar with Chat AI will have an easier way, but it’s what worked for me. With Chat AI IMO it’s all about asking it the right questions with as much detail, information, & examples u can give it.

**Example**:

Now that I have a working process to create many successful trade settings contained in each symbol's strategy's \*\*\*\* method...  
	1. What metrics should I be collecting and using to determine a trade setting(CandleEntryConfig) is no longer profitable and/or the pattern is longer valid in the market? Keep in mind the Live Trade Objectives are making more money with losing as little money as possible and keeping the drawdown as low as possible...  
		A. Profit Factor? - I like this idea as it seems key to my Live Objectives.  
		B. Return To Drawdown(ReturnToDD)? - I feel like this fits my Live Objectives as well.  
	...

The agent I am creating has access to ML derived fundamental, technical, and seasonality analysis. It also has the ability to backtest strategies. It is not released yet but you will be able to try it soon at https://yrobot.us

comments.author: SiriusAF
comments.body:
I built two trading systems with chatGPT that worked well enough to validate the process, but I’ve parked them for now while I test a sports betting model. Currently running a 100-bet test/tweak cycle and it’s profitable so far.
My advice: don’t start by asking Claude to build you a fully automated money machine.
Build a semi-manual system first inside projects. Put the framework, rules, research, testing and journaling inside a Project. Run it yourself, find the weak points, tighten the logic, and only automate once the process is actually stable.
AI is much better at helping you build and refine a system than magically discovering the edge for you.

comments.author: BFitch85
comments.body:
Yeah, I built and shipped a product with it. Full disclosure up front: it's mine, so take the plug with the appropriate salt.

It's a Windows desktop app that pairs Claude with a Robinhood or Public account. The agent researches the market and proposes stock and options trades, and you approve them. Solo build: Electron front end, a licensing server, Stripe billing, a mobile companion for approving trades from your phone, code-signed installer, the lot.

On the actual question, what surprised me is that Claude was least useful where I expected it to be most useful. Scaffolding, boilerplate, test harnesses, refactors, it's genuinely fast. But the bugs that actually cost me time were cross-system ones it couldn't see: a token minted by an older version of my server that a newer client silently misread, a CSS specificity collision, an email path that reported success while delivering nothing. Those need someone holding the whole system in their head.

Advice if you're going to try it:

Verify everything it tells you. I've had it write tests that passed with the implementation deleted. Now I delete the fix and confirm the test actually fails before I trust it.

The AI part is not the hard part. Distribution, code signing, licensing, billing and support are, and none of that gets easier because you used an LLM.

Build the boring safety scaffolding early. Guardrails, an audit log, a simulation mode. Especially if real money is involved.

If you want to poke at it, paper mode is free with no account and no card, so you can run the whole thing against live market data with simulated fills before deciding anything. [trelictech.com](http://trelictech.com)

comments.author: julys_rose
comments.body: Not a trading bot, but I've been making money with Claude in a more boring and more reliable way. My store runs on Omnisend, which has MCP support, so I connect Claude directly to my campaign and automation data. Instead of exporting reports, and trying to make sense of them manually, I just ask it things like which flows are actually driving revenue, where people are dropping off, which segments are underperforming. It pulls the real numbers and helps me think through what to do with them. The decisions I've made from those conversations have paid off in actual revenue.

comments.author: d3xinho
comments.body:
Well, depends on what you mean by "Claude". 
Yes I've made money with Sonnet 4.5 and 4.6, but using it as my LLM model in Cod3x. 

I've also made money with Qwen and Deepseek, but that's probably because the strategy I ran was good to start with until my alpha decayed. 

Claude can probably make you money for a while, but it can also ruin you, these models are not completely optimised for finance and trading. They're good enough to follow rules so you can automate your strat tho.
